analysis.title: GS Basics Brazil. What Will Break. Extreme Breadth
key_insights: September NFP was described as about as benign as it gets: softer payrolls, unemployment up, participation improved. This takes heat out of the near-term Fed path and drove further curve steepening.

Energy remains fragile, with threatened escalation and more tankers hit. Diplomatic pathways remain open and oil is getting out of the Gulf, which keeps the extreme energy tail from worsening for now. Oil is slightly lower this morning.
TSMC rose 3% in Taiwan to a clean new all-time high ahead of September sales. Privorotsky reads the foundry breakout as a signal that the AI trade is probably not a fade.

EUR is weak on a possible Spain snap election, but France is the bigger issue. OAT/Bund spread widening and fiscal anxiety are feeding into the currency. This week hinges on whether alternative French candidates can offer a credible path back to fiscal sustainability. Lane speaks this morning.

Sentiment is washed out: CNN Fear/Greed in the 30s, AAII Bull/Bear at -11.5, GS sentiment indicator at -0.7 standard deviations. Fundamental L/S funds cut almost 2 points of gross last week, and US fundamental net exposure sits around the 2nd percentile of the last 5 years. Some funds sold tech to cover macro shorts.

Breadth is split. More than half the Russell is 20% off its highs while Nasdaq is breaking out. Breadth gives little reliable forward signal, but three months later the market has historically been higher and midterm seasonals from here are supportive.

Brazil first-round polling shows Flavio Bolsonaro 47.0% and Lula 45.2%, substantially better for the market than expected. Brazil should be up a lot today and the market will front load the second round. This should initially support BRL, domestic equities and risk assets across the region, and he suggests looking at second-order Brazil plays in Europe.

Rates: last week's steepener had a lot go right for the front end (softer core PCE, supportive Williams and Jefferson comments, NFP below consensus). It was not the bull steepener hoped for given how much the back end has already sold off. A steeper curve can coexist with a more supportive Fed path if the market still expects strong nominal growth, spending and earnings.
Credit calmed at the end of last week, but HY and CCC need close monitoring.

AI: TSMC and Terafab chatter supports semis. Nvidia-backed Reflection AI is reportedly preparing its first open-weight frontier model, which could compete with the strongest Chinese open-weight models. New models are arriving roughly every ten days. Samsung preliminary numbers and TSMC September sales come Thursday.

Treasury supply is a watch item after recently mediocre auctions: $58bn 3yr Tuesday, $39bn 10yr Wednesday, $22bn 30yr Thursday. ISM Services today will show whether it confirms the rapid price acceleration seen in last week's manufacturing data.

Risk view: after the big Nasdaq rally it is sensible to sell a little into strength. But positioning is still extremely light, macro shorts are large and Russell positioning is near the bottom of its recent range, which he sees as setting up a market that grinds higher. His view changes if sentiment turns euphoric or positioning gets stretched.
Remaining concerns are energy (the key tail), France and European sovereign risk, and Eastern Europe. Q3 earnings season is close and he expects very good numbers.
earnings_insights: Privorotsky expects Q3 2026 earnings season, starting soon, to produce very good numbers (no figures given).
Samsung preliminary results and TSMC September sales are due Thursday, flagged as hard data for the semiconductor complex.
